brief: Goldman Sachs previews Q3 2026 earnings, which begin the week of October 12 with roughly 70% of S&P 500 market cap reporting by month end. Consensus expects 27% year/year EPS growth, a deceleration from Q2's 33% but still the highest pre-season estimate since 2021; GS argues neither macro data nor AI investment signals point to a Q3 slowdown, setting up another quarter of above-consensus results. Growth is narrow: Info Tech and Energy combine for nearly 80% of the gain and their median stocks grow EPS over 30%, AI infrastructure stocks drive more than half of total growth, and Micron and Nvidia alone account for over a third, while consumer-sector EPS is flat and market breadth sits at its narrowest since the Dot Com Bubble. Hyperscaler capex consensus is 116% y/y, up from 87% in Q2, and cloud revenue growth is expected to accelerate from 48% to 55%. Two one-off tailwinds fade: the roughly $150bn 'other income' boost from appreciating equity stakes (12% of Q2 EPS) and tariff refunds, which still add about 6% to quarterly pre-tax profits.
